lang.name: English
verdict.notEstablished: Not clearly established. The data do not give strong evidence of a steady trend here (grade {g}).
verdict.shiftTail: A single straight line may not describe this record well.
verdict.aiWording: AI-assisted wording; numbers come from the analysis.
case.title: Is Kumasi really getting hotter?
case.intro: People in Kumasi say the days feel hotter and the rains less reliable. We asked NASA's satellite record.
case.clue.title: The clue
case.clue.body: A feeling is not evidence. Hot weeks stand out in memory, and one year can be unusual. To know whether a place is really changing, we need decades of measurements and a fair test.
case.evidence.title: The evidence
case.evidence.body: Monthly air temperature over Kumasi, with the seasons removed so only the long-term change is left. The thick line is the trend.
case.twist.title: The twist
case.twist.body: Rainfall tells a different story. Over the same city the answer is less clear, and across West Africa some places are getting wetter while others are getting drier.
case.verdict.title: The verdict
case.cannot.title: What we cannot say
case.cannot.cause: Why it is changing. A significant trend does not identify its cause.
case.cannot.shape: Whether the change is a straight line. This tool detects monotonic trends only; real changes can be non-linear or cyclical.
case.cannot.future: What happens next. These are past trends, not forecasts.
